facts.text: Mount Tabor was named after the biblical mountain where Christ’s Transfiguration occurred, chosen by a Methodist camp meeting group in the 19th century.
The town’s streets wind through Victorian cottages with gingerbread trim and bright period paint, creating a colorful architectural adventure.
In 2015, Mount Tabor’s historic district earned a spot on both the National and New Jersey Registers of Historic Places.
The Ebenezer Pavilion, once an open‑air prayer space, now houses the smallest branch of the Parsippany‑Troy Hills library system.
A parking lot was added to Main Park in the 1950s to accommodate the growing number of visitors arriving by car.
The Newark Conference Camp Meeting Association began holding annual Methodist camp meetings at Lake Speedwell in 1866 before relocating to Mount Tabor.
